original.reason: The proof assumes selected blocks are four consecutive integers, which is generally false after prior sum deletions. Its deletion argument is also invalid: infinitely many deletions can each disrupt a different proposed block, so it does not establish that infinitely many such blocks are selected.

judgment.reason: The claim is not proved. The described front movement and coset switching do not imply that all window-sum residues are visited, nor is the effect of skips on the actual nonconsecutive front entries justified.

The “residue-sweep lemma” is asserted with unsupported claims. In particular, skips do not merely preserve a sweep through every residue, and the varying deleted sums and resulting gaps are not controlled.

Its circuit argument is undefined and incorrect: a complete circuit does not ‘change the sum ... by 4,’ and the effect of an extra erasure is not represented by a simple mark. Thus the asserted sweep of all residues does not follow.

The additional deletion is not shown to cause only an adjacent transposition of front windows. Consequently the assertions about parity cosets and a pair of sweeps containing every residue are unsupported, so the residue-sweep principle is unproved.
